title: Mixture-of-Agents Enhances Large Language Model Capabilities
authors: Junlin Wang, Jue Wang, Ben Athiwaratkun, Ce Zhang, James Zou
abstract-summary: Layered MoA architecture where each layer has multiple LLM agents taking outputs from previous layer as auxiliary info
notes: MoA with open-source LLMs surpasses GPT-4o; also SOTA on MT-Bench and FLASK

title: MetaGPT: Meta Programming for A Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework
authors: Sirui Hong, Mingchen Zhuge, Jonathan Chen, Xiawu Zheng, Yuheng Cheng, others
abstract-summary: Multi-agent framework encoding SOPs into prompts with roles like product manager and engineer for software dev
notes: Executability score 3.9 vs ChatDev 2.1 on SoftwareDev; 100% task completion rate

title: ChatDev: Communicative Agents for Software Development
authors: Chen Qian, Xin Cong, Wei Liu, Cheng Yang, Weize Chen, others
abstract-summary: Virtual software company with CEO/CTO/programmer/tester roles collaborating via chat for end-to-end software development
notes: Score of 1.0 for AutoGPT baseline; ChatDev outperforms single-agent but underperforms MetaGPT

title: CAMEL: Communicative Agents for Mind Exploration of Large Language Model Society
authors: Guohao Li, Hasan Hammoud, Hani Itani, Dmitrii Khizbullin, Bernard Ghanem
abstract-summary: Role-playing framework using inception prompting for autonomous multi-agent cooperation and data generation
notes: Primarily a framework paper; generated datasets used to fine-tune models that surpass LLaMA-7B and Vicuna-7B

title: AgentVerse: Facilitating Multi-Agent Collaboration and Exploring Emergent Behaviors
authors: Weize Chen, Yusheng Su, Jingwei Zuo, Cheng Yang, Chenfei Yuan, others
abstract-summary: Four-stage multi-agent framework (recruit/decide/execute/evaluate) showing emergent collaborative behaviors
notes: Multi-agent outperforms single agent across tasks; GPT-3.5 collaboration can be vulnerable to incorrect info

title: Improving Factuality and Reasoning in Language Models through Multiagent Debate
authors: Yilun Du, Shuang Li, Antonio Torralba, Joshua Tenenbaum, Igor Mordatch
abstract-summary: Multiple LLM instances debate over multiple rounds to reach consensus on reasoning and factuality tasks
notes: 17/20 vs 14/20 on GSM subset; also improves on MMLU and biography generation factuality

title: Encouraging Divergent Thinking in Large Language Models through Multi-Agent Debate
authors: Tian Liang, Zhiwei He, Wenxiang Jiao, Xing Wang, Yan Wang, others
abstract-summary: MAD framework with tit-for-tat debate and judge to address Degeneration-of-Thought problem
notes: Also achieves COMET 82.0 on Common MT surpassing GPT-4 baseline; addresses DoT problem in self-reflection

title: Single-Agent LLMs Outperform Multi-Agent Systems on Multi-Hop Reasoning Under Equal Thinking Token Budgets
authors: Dat Tran, Douwe Kiela
abstract-summary: Information-theoretic argument via Data Processing Inequality that single agents are more efficient under fixed token budgets
notes: Single agent matches or outperforms MA in nearly every condition under equal compute; key methodological critique

title: MultiAgentBench: Evaluating the Collaboration and Competition of LLM Agents
authors: Kunlun Zhu, Hongyi Du, Zhaochen Hong, Xiaocheng Yang, Shuyi Guo, others
abstract-summary: Comprehensive benchmark with milestone-based KPIs for cooperative and competitive multi-agent scenarios
notes: Graph topology performs best; cognitive planning improves milestone rates by 3%; evaluates star/chain/tree/graph topologies

title: DyLAN: A Dynamic LLM-Powered Agent Network for Task-Oriented Agent Collaboration
authors: Zijun Liu, Yanzhe Zhang, Peng Li, Yang Liu, Diyi Yang
abstract-summary: Dynamic agent network with Agent Importance Score for adaptive team selection across tasks
notes: 13.3% improvement on HumanEval; 10.2% improvement over LLM Debate with 36.6% API calls; also improves MMLU by up to 25%

title: Self-Collaboration Code Generation via ChatGPT
authors: Yihong Dong, Xue Jiang, Zhi Jin, Ge Li
abstract-summary: Three-role team (analyst/coder/tester) for code generation via self-collaboration of single LLM
notes: 29.9-47.1% relative improvement; coder-tester team achieves 36.7% and 39.4% improvements on MBPP and MBPP-ET

title: MapCoder: Multi-Agent Code Generation for Competitive Problem Solving
authors: Md. Ashraful Islam, Mohammed Latif Siddiq, Joanna C.S. Santos
abstract-summary: Four-agent framework emulating program synthesis cycle: recall/plan/generate/debug
notes: Also 83.1% on MBPP; 22.0% on APPS; 28.5% on CodeContests; SOTA across 7 benchmarks

title: AgentCoder: Multi-Agent-based Code Generation with Iterative Testing and Optimisation
authors: Dong Huang, Jie M. Zhang, Michael Luck, Qingwen Bu, Yuhao Qing, Heming Cui
abstract-summary: Three specialized agents (programmer/test designer/test executor) with iterative testing and optimization
notes: 91.8% on MBPP vs 78.9% SOTA; average 91.5% with GPT-4 and 84.1% with GPT-3.5 across datasets

title: ReConcile: Round-Table Conference Improves Reasoning via Consensus among Diverse LLMs
authors: Justin Chen, Swarnadeep Saha, Mohit Bansal
abstract-summary: Multi-model round-table conference with confidence-weighted voting for consensus reasoning
notes: Surpasses GPT-4 on 3 datasets; 8% improvement on MATH; heterogeneous model team

title: Corex: Pushing the Boundaries of Complex Reasoning through Multi-Model Collaboration
authors: Qiushi Sun, Zhangyue Yin, Xiang Li, Zhiyong Wu, Xipeng Qiu, Lingpeng Kong
abstract-summary: Suite of multi-model collaboration strategies: Discuss/Review/Retrieve modes for complex reasoning
notes: Three collaboration paradigms that transform LLMs into autonomous agents; outperforms single-agent baselines

title: Beyond the Strongest LLM: Multi-Turn Multi-Agent Orchestration vs. Single LLMs on Benchmarks
authors: Xue et al.
abstract-summary: Multi-turn voting/debate orchestration among frontier LLMs compared to individual model performance
backbone-model: Gemini 2.5 Pro / GPT-5 / Grok 4 / Claude Sonnet 4
notes: Best single model (Grok 4) achieves 90.6% but orchestration matches or exceeds on average across 3 benchmarks

title: Stop Overvaluing Multi-Agent Debate -- We Must Rethink Evaluation and Embrace Model Heterogeneity
authors: Zhang et al.
abstract-summary: Systematic evaluation of 5 MAD methods across 9 benchmarks with 4 models; finds MAD often fails to beat CoT/SC
notes: MAD often fails to outperform simple CoT and Self-Consistency baselines; model heterogeneity is key improvement

title: Talk Structurally Act Hierarchically: A Collaborative Framework for LLM Multi-Agent Systems
authors: Shubham Patel, Qingyun Wang, others
abstract-summary: Structured communication protocol with hierarchical refinement system for multi-agent task solving
notes: Surpasses OpenAI-o1 and AgentVerse and single-agent ReAct baselines; both structured communication and hierarchical refinement are essential

title: SWE-Search: Enhancing Software Agents with Monte Carlo Tree Search and Iterative Refinement
authors: Antonis Antoniades, Albert Örwall, Kexun Zhang, Yuxi Xie, Anirudh Goyal, William Wang
abstract-summary: Multi-agent MCTS framework with SWE-Agent / Value Agent / Discriminator Agent for software engineering
notes: 23% relative improvement over standard open-source agents across 5 models; multi-agent debate for decision-making

title: How to Train a Leader: Hierarchical Reasoning in Multi-Agent LLMs
authors: Abdelnabi et al.
abstract-summary: MLPO trains a leader LLM to coordinate untrained peer agents; outperforms debate and self-reflection baselines
notes: Leader trained with MLPO also improves in single-agent settings; outperforms MAD and Self-Reflection under fixed 40-generation budget

title: MAR: Multi-Agent Reflexion Improves Reasoning Abilities in LLMs
authors: Yang et al.
abstract-summary: Multi-agent reflexion with actor + 4 critic personas + judge for structured diverse feedback
notes: Also +3 EM on HotPotQA (44->47); separates acting/diagnosing/critiquing/aggregating to reduce confirmation bias

title: M3MAD-Bench: Are Multi-Agent Debates Really Effective Across Domains and Modalities?
authors: Liao et al.
abstract-summary: Unified benchmark for MAD across 5 task domains with text and vision-language datasets and efficiency metrics
notes: Systematic cross-modality comparison; reveals performance-cost trade-offs; standardizes MAD evaluation protocols

title: DReaMAD: From Belief Entrenchment to Robust Reasoning in LLM Agents
authors: Li et al.
abstract-summary: Addresses belief entrenchment in MAD via strategic prior knowledge elicitation and perspective diversity
notes: +19.0% higher win rate than standard MAD; addresses root causes of homogenized debate dynamics

title: BattleAgentBench: Evaluating Cooperation and Competition Capabilities of Language Models in Multi-Agent Systems
authors: Zhao et al.
abstract-summary: Seven sub-stages at three difficulty levels evaluating single-agent navigation / paired-agent execution / multi-agent cooperation
notes: API-based models show some cooperative ability but large room for improvement; open-source models struggle on simple tasks
